title: The Hindu Code Bill: Sacrificing Cabinet Office for Women's Rights
summary: The only Law Minister in world history to resign his cabinet seat over the defense of women's inheritance and divorce rights, proving that principle matters infinitely more than power.
keywords: The Hindu Code Bill: Sacrificing Cabinet Office for Women's Rights
full_text:
Following independence, Dr. B. R. Ambedkar assumed office as independent India's first Law Minister in Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru's cabinet.

His masterpiece as Law Minister was the **Hindu Code Bill**—a revolutionary reform aimed at liberating Indian women from centuries of legal disenfranchisement:
1. Daughters received an equal share in ancestral property alongside sons.
2. Polygamy was outlawed, establishing strict monogamy.
3. Women received the legal right to petition for divorce from abusive marriages.
4. Inter-caste marriages and inter-caste adoptions were legalized.

However, conservative forces inside and outside parliament erupted in furious revolt. Orthodox parliamentarians filibustered the bill, shouting: "Ambedkar is destroying the sanctity of the traditional family! He wants to encourage western divorces!"

Fearing electoral fallout in the impending 1952 general elections, Nehru decided to stall the bill.

Ambedkar addressed Parliament with fiery indignation:
"Honorable members! You gladly grant succession rights to the heirs of rajas and maharajas; why do you tremble at the thought of granting equal property rights to your own daughters?
A husband is free to abandon his wife, yet you demand that an abused woman must suffer silently until the funeral pyre!
How can a nation boast of democratic freedom when half its population remains enslaved within its own households?"

When the cabinet shelved the bill, Ambedkar took an astonishing step.

On September 27, 1951, he submitted his resignation as Law Minister.

In his resignation address, Ambedkar stated:
"I did not enter this government to enjoy ministerial perquisites or power. I came to secure justice for the oppressed and to bestow equal rights upon the women of India.
Since this parliament refuses to emancipate its daughters, my conscience forbids me from remaining a minister for another hour!"

He walked out of the corridors of power with his head held high.

Ambedkar remains the only minister in modern history to resign cabinet office exclusively for the cause of women's emancipation. Years later, parliament was forced to pass the Hindu Code in piecemeal acts, validating Ambedkar's visionary reforms.
moral: Power and office are meaningful only as instruments for justice; walking away from power when principles are compromised is the mark of supreme integrity.
witty_quote: I measure the progress of a community by the degree of progress which women have achieved!

He was appointed to the Supreme Court
